Tafsir al-Jalalayn, on Surah 97 (al-Qadr), verse 1:

﴿Indeed, We revealed it﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, all at once, from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya), ﴿during the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr)﴾ i.e., the Night of Great Honor (al-Sharaf al-'Azim).

Qur'anic quotations: "And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?" (Q 97:2)

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "And what made you know" (wa-ma adraka) means: what informed you, O Muhammad, "what is the Night of Decree" (laylat al-qadr)? It is an exaltation of its status and an expression of wonder at it.

Quranic quotation: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.﴾ It is better than a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree, so righteous deeds performed in it are better than those performed in a thousand months that lack it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 97, verse 4:

﴿The angels descend﴾, with one of the two taa' elided from the original (tatanazzalu), ﴿and the Spirit﴾, i.e., Jibril (Gabriel), ﴿therein﴾, in the night, ﴿by the permission of their Lord﴾, by His command, ﴿with every decree﴾ which Allah has decreed therein for that year until the next. Min (from) here is causal, in the sense of bi (by, with).

ليلة القدر: 5 — "سَلَامٌ هِيَ حَتَّى مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ"

Translation of the commentary:

﴿Peace it is﴾: it is a predicate placed first (khabar muqaddam) and the subject (mubtada') follows it. ﴿Until the rising of the dawn﴾: with the lam pronounced with a fatha and with a kasra, meaning until the time of its rising. It was described as "peace" because of the abundance of peace in it from the angels, who pass by every believing man and every believing woman and greet them with peace.
